No — it's problem "Sum of the array beauty": For each subsequence of length k, beauty = min |nums[i]-nums[j]| over consecutive elements in sorted subsequence. Sum beauty over all subsequences.

The algorithm: sort nums, compute all pairwise differences, iterate mn from largest to smallest, count subsequences of length k where all adjacent differences >= mn, dp computed with the jump pointer j being the smallest index such that nums[i]-nums[j] < mn, so dp counts subsequences ending at i including dp[j][l-1] where indices <= j-1... Actually j is the first index where nums[i]-nums[j] < mn, meaning indices j..i-1 all have nums[i]-nums[j'] >= mn (they can precede i). So dp[i+1][l] += dp[j][l-1] counts subsequences of length l with last element i and all adjacent differences >= mn. Then dp[i+1][l] += dp[i][l] accumulates prefix sums (subsequences not using i). Then cnt = dp[n][k] - prev where prev is count for previous (larger) mn. This cnt counts subsequences whose min adjacent diff is exactly >= mn but not >= prev mn, i.e., beauty exactly mn? Hmm, count of subsequences with min diff >= mn minus count with min diff >= previous larger mn gives subsequences with min diff in [mn, prev), which is exactly mn since mn values are the pairwise differences. So beauty = mn. Result = sum over subsequences of beauty.
